name: Amin Eldery
title: Computer Systems Engineering Student
about: I'm a fourth-year Computer Systems Engineering student at Carleton University. I like working close to the hardware: writing Verilog for FPGAs, embedded C on microcontrollers, and C++ for robots that have to react in real time.

On my co-op at Terra Motion Canada I worked on the other end of the stack, building Python and C++ tools for satellite radar data and shipping them as Docker containers on AWS. I enjoy both sides, and I'm happiest when a project needs the two to meet.

education.degree: Bachelor of Computer Systems Engineering, Co-op Option

bullets: Developed two analysis tools in Python, C++, and MATLAB for Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data processing and resolved software issues caused by evolving satellite data formats.
Containerized 6 Python/C++ services using Docker and supported deployment on AWS (ECR, S3, Lambda), improving deployment consistency and scalability.
Optimized software packaging using Nuitka and developed test cases to validate containerized applications and ensure deployment reliability.
Configured and maintained Proxmox VE workstations by provisioning Linux virtual machines and troubleshooting virtualization and networking issues.
Collaborated with cross-functional engineers using Git and GitLab to implement features, debug production issues, and enhance software performance.
Administered and supported Dentrix software across multiple dental clinic environments.
Troubleshot hardware, software, networking, and dental imaging system issues through remote support.
Maintained Windows server infrastructure, user accounts, backups, and secure remote access services.
Managed Microsoft 365, including Exchange, SharePoint, and Entra ID (Azure AD) administration.

projects.name: Autonomous Snowplow Robot
bullets: Designing an autonomous robot that clears simulated snow from a taped indoor arena using a boustrophedon sweep, avoiding static and moving obstacles under a 25 cm/s speed cap and 5-minute run limit.

Own the mechanical and boundary subsystem: a custom 220 mm plow, a 3-channel line follower for tape detection, and an encoder-driven push-out routine that keeps the wheels within 3 cm of the boundary.

Co-authored 17 measurable requirements and a 10-state, 16-transition control state machine fusing IMU, encoder, ToF, ultrasonic, Sharp IR and digital IR sensors, with a watchdog, battery-voltage fault detection and an RGB status LED driven over UART.

projects.name: MetroBeacon
bullets: Built a campus transit-assistance system delivering real-time OC Transpo bus and train arrivals through a mobile app, LED indicators, and a Raspberry Pi Sense HAT display.
Ingested live GTFS-RT trip updates and vehicle positions in Python and published them to a Firebase Realtime Database for cross-device access.
Developed a React Native (Expo) GUI with dark mode, accessibility, and multilingual support, alongside a GPIO-driven LED map and button-triggered arrival feedback on hardware.

projects.name: FPGA Ethernet Packet Processing Engine
bullets: Designed an FPGA-based Ethernet packet processor in Verilog on the Zybo Z7-20, implementing FSMs, FIFOs, and packet parsing logic.
Implemented CRC generation and validation to ensure reliable packet transmission and data integrity.
Verified functionality using Vivado simulations and self-checking testbenches while analyzing timing closure and FPGA resource utilization.

projects.name: GPU & ASIC Mining Farm
bullets: Built and operated a 40-GPU mining farm (AMD RX 5700 XT) and 2 Bitmain Antminer T9 ASICs, handling hardware assembly, PCIe riser wiring, electrical circuit planning and power distribution.
Managed the full fleet remotely through HiveOS (Linux), tuning per-card clocks, voltages and memory timings for efficiency and stability, with monitoring and alerts for fast fault response.

Designed the cooling, airflow and network setup, and diagnosed hardware and software faults such as failing risers, unstable overclocks and rig crashes to keep uptime high over two years of continuous operation.

projects.name: Real-Time Traffic Light Controller
bullets: Designed a real-time traffic light controller in Embedded C on the MSP432, implementing interrupt-driven pedestrian crossing and timer-based state transitions.
Configured GPIO, timers, NVIC interrupts, and debouncing to ensure reliable real-time operation.
Developed modular firmware drivers and validated functionality using Keil µVision and on-board debugging tools.
